subject: Configurable TTL per tenant + geo-zone routing questions
messages:
From: Dana Liu <dana.liu@acme-corp.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: security@acme-corp.com
Date: 2027-03-14T09:12:00Z
Subject: Tenant-level retention + regional routing questions

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. A couple of follow-ups from our security and infra teams as we evaluate Redwood for our PII workloads:

1) We need per-tenant configurable TTLs so that different products under Acme can set retention windows (30d, 1y, 7y) without impacting others. Can Redwood support tenant-level TTLs that are enforced at the storage layer?

2) For EU-resident customers, legal requires that data at rest be stored in an EU region. Is there a way to route specific tenants or datasets to EU storage even if the compute lives in the US? What does that look like operationally (buckets, encryption keys)?

3) Auditability: we need deletion proofs (audit trail) when a TTL expires or a retention override is applied. Is there an API or an export we can pull for audits?

Attaching a simplified data map that shows which tenant belongs to which product. Happy to jump on a quick call if it's easier.

Dana
Director, Security Evaluations
Acme Corp

Attachment: acme_data_map.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Dana Liu <dana.liu@acme-corp.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, grace.oconnor@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2027-03-14T14:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Tenant-level retention + regional routing questions

Hi Dana — thanks for the clear list and the attachment. High-level answers up front, then a short plan: 

- Tenant-level TTLs: Yes, supported conceptually. We can surface per-tenant retention settings in the control plane. Enforcement can be implemented at the storage layer by assigning retention metadata on persisted objects and running coordinated deletion jobs.

- Geo routing: We support routing storage to region-scoped buckets (e.g., eu-west-1) and customer-managed KMS keys per region. Compute can still live in the US, but the payloads will be encrypted and written to region-specific storage. We call this "storage-residency routing".

- Audit/deletion proofs: We can emit deletion events to the audit log and produce exportable runbooks (and signed manifests) for deletions. We already have a prototype that generates a signed JSON manifest pointing to tombstone entries.

Plan: I want to pull in engineering to scope the work and provide an implementation approach and ETA. Karthik, Grace, Lauren — can you review the attachment and tell me which approach looks feasible for an initial MVP (low-risk guarantees) vs. a full product solution (multi-tenant per-region isolation)?

Dana — I'll schedule a 30-min follow-up next week once we have a short proposal.

Thanks,
Priyom
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Date: 2027-03-15T10:18:00Z
Subject: Internal: scoping tenant TTL + geo-residency MVP (ACME)

Team — forwarding Acme's data map and requirements (attached). Key asks: per-tenant TTLs, option to pin storage of specific tenants to EU, and deletion audit manifests.

Goal: a pragmatic MVP that is low operational risk and can be offered to enterprise customers in the next quarter. Options to evaluate: 

A) Metadata-managed TTLs + periodic deletion job (fast): store data with retention metadata and run a cluster job to delete expired objects. Storage remains shared but deletions are enforced. Pros: simple. Cons: does not satisfy regions-with-hard-sovereignty by itself.

B) Region-scoped buckets + routing at write time (medium): route tenant writes to region-specific object stores and use per-region KMS. Pros: clear residency. Cons: more complex for prefix-level caching and KV cache coordination across regions.

C) Tenant-isolated storage + compute (heavy): full isolation per tenant (separate infra). Pros: strongest guarantees. Cons: operational cost.

Questions for engineering: 
- Karthik: for option B, can we keep a global KV cache while ensuring that persisted tokens/objects are written to region buckets? How painful is the routing layer change?
- Grace: what audit artifacts can we generate today (signed manifests, retention-change events)? Can we version these exports for compliance?
- Lauren: any product-facing UI/role required for tenant-level TTL controls and overrides?

Please reply with feasibility notes and rough engineering level-of-effort (S, M, L). I'll consolidate and share back with Acme.

-- Priyom

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, grace.oconnor@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2027-03-16T15:24:00Z
Subject: Re: Internal: scoping tenant TTL + geo-residency MVP (ACME)

Thanks for the summary. Quick feasibility notes: 

- Option A (metadata + deletion job): S. We already have deletion runners and prefix metadata tagging; shipping this as a configurable TTL per tenant is ~2 weeks of work to add controls + tests. Audit artifacts: we can log deletion events to the audit stream (already exists) and produce manifests from those logs.

- Option B (region-scoped buckets + routing): M. Routing writes by tenant to region buckets is doable. Main complexity is the write path change and ensuring consistency of cached KV entries (we'd need to include a storage-region tag in the KV keyspace so cache lookups are region-aware). My estimate: 4-6 weeks for a guarded rollout (feature flag + canary tenants). KMS integration per region is straightforward (we have KMS connectors).

- Option C (tenant isolation): L. This is effectively dedicated infra and will require separate infra provisioning and network controls — not ideal for quick wins.

Engineering asks: 1) product to define the default behavior for mixed-tenant workloads (compute in US but storage pinned to EU) and 2) legal to specify the level of "residency proof" required (signed manifests vs. on-demand exports).

I'll open a Jira ticket (INF-8421) for Option B scoping and attach a small spike for Option A.

Karthik
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
